program: Wingless fixed-budget future-data learning-efficiency signal validation
question: Does a training-only representation-headroom signal predict which sealed future domain requires more equal-budget adaptation data to improve held-out prediction at fixed capacity?
hypothesis: Run three leave-one-domain-out arms over the exact original external manifest. Before opening any target bytes, use the same 15,819-byte proportional non-target training budget and fixed 256-motif capacity from R2/R3. Compute one frozen native signal only: representation_headroom = eligible_motif_count_before_truncation - 256. Then freeze the signal and open a common 1,454-byte target window per domain. The first 872 target bytes are an adaptation stream divided into eight cumulative 109-byte packets; the final 582 bytes are sealed evaluation. At packet 0 and after each packet, rebuild the fixed-capacity representation/relation model from the unchanged non-target base plus the revealed target prefix and evaluate the same deterministic next-motif prediction metric on the 582-byte sealed suffix. Define packets_to_first_gain as the first packet whose exact-hit count exceeds packet-0 by at least one; failure value 9. The hypothesis predicts lower training-only headroom -> greater packets_to_first_gain. No candidate modification is selected or retained.

portfolio_context.role: advisory-only; primary objective is efficient learning of unseen future data under fixed budgets

prior_evidence.interpretation: The bounded bridge condition changed behavior without improving task performance; per contract, stop optimizing that originating-dataset mechanism and return to native signals for future-data learning efficiency.

external_authority.execution_host_policy: GitHub-hosted compute only; host distinct from LINKDEADKB

fixed_budget.non_target_allocation_rule: same proportional exact-prefix rule as R2/R3
fixed_budget.compute_rule: same deterministic fixed-capacity representation/relation rebuild and evaluator at every packet; no extra runtime for any arm

signal.name: representation_headroom
signal.definition: eligible_motif_count_before_truncation - 256 using non-target training bytes only
signal.lower_means: less representational support and predicted slower future adaptation

evaluation.metric: deterministic next-motif exact-hit count on sealed evaluation using the fixed-capacity learned relation model
evaluation.packets_to_first_gain: first packet 1..8 with exact hits >= packet0+1; otherwise 9
evaluation.rank_test: For every pair of arms with unequal representation_headroom and unequal packets_to_first_gain, count agreement when lower headroom has greater packets_to_first_gain. supported requires at least 2 agreeing pairwise comparisons and zero reversed comparisons; ties are neutral.

classification_rules.supported: Validity passes; representation headroom correctly orders at least two pairwise future-adaptation comparisons with zero reversals under equal budgets.
classification_rules.mixed: Validity passes; at least one pair agrees and at least one pair reverses or too many ties prevent the supported criterion.
classification_rules.negative: Validity passes but there is no agreeing non-tied pair or reversals dominate.
classification_rules.invalid: Any parent, authority, source, budget, split, signal-freeze, evaluator identity, deterministic replay, capacity, provenance, or qualification criterion fails.

successor_if_supported.intent: test whether a preregistered fixed total data budget allocated using the validated training-only headroom signal improves aggregate learning across multiple unseen future datasets versus equal allocation; no self-modification

successor_if_mixed_or_negative.intent: factor representation headroom, class-support deficit, and relation-margin statistics prospectively under the same fixed adaptation budgets before any allocation policy

no_post_result_tuning_rule: Do not alter source identities, 15,819-byte base budget, 256 capacity, 1,454-byte target window, 872/582 split, eight 109-byte packets, signal formula, evaluator, packet gain rule, rank test, metrics, thresholds, classification, or authority after primary output.
